'''Jamaica''' is a [[neighborhood]] in the [[Boroughs of New York City|New York City borough]] of [[Queens]]. Jamaica is bordered by [[Hollis, Queens|Hollis]], [[Queens Village, Queens|Queens Village]], [[St. Albans, Queens|St. Albans]], and [[Cambria Heights, Queens|Cambria Heights]] to the east; [[South Jamaica, Queens|South Jamaica]], [[Rochdale Village, Queens|Rochdale Village]], [[John F. Kennedy International Airport]], and [[Springfield Gardens, Queens|Springfield Gardens]] to the south; [[Laurelton, Queens|Laurelton]] and [[Rosedale, Queens|Rosedale]] to the southeast; [[Richmond Hill, Queens|Richmond Hill]], [[South Ozone Park]], and [[Aqueduct Racetrack]] to the west and southwest; [[Briarwood, Queens|Briarwood]] to the northwest; and [[Kew Gardens Hills, Queens|Kew Gardens Hills]], [[Jamaica Hills, Queens|Jamaica Hills]], and [[Jamaica Estates, Queens|Jamaica Estates]] to the north.

Jamaica may get its name from ''Yameco'', a corruption of a word for "beaver" in the [[Delaware languages|Lenape language]] spoken by the Native Americans who lived in the area at the time of first European contact.<ref name="Pollak 2014">{{cite web | title=What Is Jamaica, Queens, Named After? | website=The New York Times | last=Pollak | first=Michael | date=July 6, 2014 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/07/06/nyregion/what-is-jamaica-queens-named-after.html | access-date=April 6, 2019}}</ref>  The liquid "y" sound of English is spelled with a "j" in Dutch, the language of the first people to write about the area; the English retained this Dutch spelling, but, after repeated reading and speaking of "Jamaica", slowly replaced the liquid sound with the hard "j" of the English pronunciation of the name today.<ref>[http://www.nycgovparks.org/sub_your_park/historical_signs/hs_historical_sign.php?id=12608 Major Mark Park], accessed December 16, 2006</ref> 

Jamaica was settled under [[Netherlands|Dutch]] rule in 1656. It was originally called ''{{lang|nl|Rustdorp}}''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://freepages.genealogy.rootsweb.com/~jdevlin/ny/jamaica_li_hist.htm |title=Jamaica |access-date=December 23, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080127133757/http://freepages.genealogy.rootsweb.com/~jdevlin/ny/jamaica_li_hist.htm |archive-date=January 27, 2008 |url-status=dead}} {{cite book |title=The History of Long Island, from its earliest settlement to the present time |url=https://archive.org/details/historylongisla00rossgoog |author=Peter Ross |location=NY |publisher=Lewis Pub. Co. |year=1902}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archive.org/details/historyoftownoff01stro|title=The history of the town of Flatbush in Kings County, Long Island|first=Thomas M. (Thomas Morris)|last=Strong|date=September 23, 1908|publisher=Brooklyn, N.Y. : F. Loeser & Co.|via=Internet Archive}}</ref> Under [[British colonization of the Americas|English rule]], Jamaica became the center of the "[[Political subdivisions of New York State#Town|Town]] of Jamaica"; the name is of [[Lenape]] origin and wholly unrelated to [[Jamaica#Etymology|that of the country]]. It was the first [[county seat]] of Queens County, holding that title from 1683 to 1788, and was the first incorporated village on [[Long Island]]. When Queens was incorporated into the [[City of Greater New York]] in 1898, both the town of Jamaica and the village of Jamaica were dissolved, but the neighborhood of Jamaica regained its role as county seat.

Jamaica is the location of several government buildings such as [[New York City Civil Court|Queens Civil Court]], the civil branch of the [[New York Supreme Court|Queens County Supreme Court]], the Queens County Family Court and the [[Joseph Patrick Addabbo|Joseph P. Addabbo]] Federal Building, home to the [[Social Security Administration]]'s Northeastern Program Service Center.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.gruzensamton.com/pdf/Addabbo.pdf|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110711132147/http://www.gruzensamton.com/pdf/Addabbo.pdf|archive-date = July 11, 2011|title = Addabbo|url-status=usurped}}</ref> The U.S. [[Food and Drug Administration]]'s Northeast Regional Laboratory as well as the New York District Office are located in Jamaica. Jamaica Center, the area around [[Jamaica Avenue]], is a major commercial center. The [[New York Racing Association]], based at [[Aqueduct Racetrack]] in South Ozone Park, lists its official address as Jamaica. Central Jamaica once housed the [[Jamaica Race Course|Jamaica Racetrack]], now the massive Rochdale Village housing development. [[John F. Kennedy International Airport]] and the hotels nearby are also located in Jamaica. The neighborhood is located in [[Queens Community Board 12|Queens Community District 12]].<ref name="NYCPlanning"/> It is patrolled by the [[New York City Police Department]]'s 103rd and 113th Precincts.
